message.content: {"summary":"Your report is well structured with balanced arguments, relevant case studies (NHS/HSSIB, Volkswagen) and clear stakeholder identification. To reach the top band, you need a compelling, consistent argument chain: fix the recommendation that contradicts your conclusion, correct factual and arithmetic errors, add the required abstract, and strengthen references and visual elements.","next_steps":["Revise the Recommendation so it aligns with your conclusion that servers should not be shipped — currently you advise accepting the health contract while also recommending delayed launches, which is internally inconsistent.","Add the required ~150-word abstract, and proofread headings and typos (e.g. 'DICUSSION', 'ofprofessional', inconsistent 'EACE' abbreviation for the Engineers Australia code).","Verify case-study facts before citing: the Volkswagen scandal involved diesel emissions cheating, not defeat devices in electric vehicles manipulating crash-safety tests; also correct 1% of 5,000 servers (50, not 500), and complete reference details (e.g. BBC URL, author names)."],"criteria":{"C1":"You identified several ethical issues (defective shipping, public safety, professional integrity) and linked them to engineering design, addressing both organisational context and stakeholders. To reach Excellent, deepen your discussion of why each issue is significant, not just that it exists.","C2":"Your for/against arguments (competitive advantage vs harm to end-users, reputation) show appropriate depth, and you drew conclusions on decision-making. Excellent requires deeper argumentation plus explicit, stakeholder-specific decision-making recommendations for several different parties.","C3":"Your body is logically ordered with case evidence, but the recommendation contradicts your conclusion (accept the contract yet delay launches), muddling the argument-to-conclusion link. Excellent requires a compelling, fully consistent argument chain demonstrating systematic understanding of issues for all stakeholders.","C4":"You used four references plus external case studies and quantitative reasoning, showing good research. However, the misdescribed Volkswagen case undermines evidentiary reliability. Excellent requires accurate, well-substantiated references with both qualitative and quantitative evidence demonstrating in-depth understanding.","C5":"Your writing is fluent overall, but the missing abstract, typos ('DICUSSION', 'ofprofessional'), no figures/tables, and incomplete references (BBC lacks URL; garbled author names) hold you back. Excellent requires several visual element types used competently and extensive, well-formatted references."}}
